steps.name: Production build and offline browser smoke

output.body:
## Summary

Add a geometry query to the retained native menu, following merged #41 and #42. Production pointer wiring follows in a separate PR.

```text
MainMenuView.hit(stagePoint, motion)
  title → block
  series → live child or background
  controls → interactive inner clip, then decoration
    AssetPack.hitClip(localPoint, full inverse transform)
```

Carry the full inverse transform into stroke contact so Play's 3.4× wrapper does not inflate its minimum stroke width. Reject static shapes outside their declared bounds before allocating contact paths.

## Evidence

- **Before:** The backlog picker reports Play at `(207.85, 213.67492904663087)` on a transient hover frame because it treats a local pixel as a Stage pixel. The new browser regression fails with that implementation.
  **After:** The corrected picker rejects the point; the same regression passes. The fixture drives hover poses from independently recorded source targets.
- Native browser checks cover all 12 target-bearing reference observations, six control corners, and child creation/removal across all 19 series frames.
- Validation: formatting, TypeScript, 475 rule tests (5,992 assertions), production build, and nine affected native/mock browser cases passed across focused runs. The negative control failed at the intended stroke assertion.
- Original artwork remains runtime supplied. Native checks require the local research SWF; hosted CI runs the existing mock/synthetic suite. Global timeline phase, exact Adobe boundaries and full game parity remain unverified.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Revert restores the previous API. No saved data or asset imports change.

**Blast Radius:** geometry

The new native-menu query has no production input caller yet. The shared static-shape bounds check uses the existing ShapeContact bounds predicate; morph contact is unchanged.
output.title: feat: query retained native menu geometry

class Bits:
 def __init__(self,b):self.b=b;self.p=0
 def u(self,n):
